description: Screenshot of the official SecureDrop Directory web page (securedrop.org), a project of Freedom of the Press Foundation, with its cube logo, a Donate button, and menu sections (FAQ, News, Directory, Demo, guides). The page text explains SecureDrop as an open-source whistleblower submission system originally coded by Aaron Swartz and advises verifying .onion addresses against the directory. At the bottom, a hand-drawn yellow circle and asterisk annotate the first directory entry, 'Apache' (https://www.apache.be/securedrop), highlighting it without stating why.
text: SECUREDROP. A project of FREEDOM OF THE PRESS FOUNDATION. Donate. Main menu. FAQ. News. Directory. Demo. The Official SecureDrop Directory. SecureDrop is an open-source whistleblower submission system that media organizations can install to securely accept documents from anonymous sources. It was originally coded by the late Aaron Swartz and is now managed by Freedom of the Press Foundation. This page contains a list of active instances. Getting started?. Guide for sources. Guide for journalists. Guide for admins. Request help. Sample privacy policy. Instance verification. If you intend to submit information to an organization's SecureDrop, we recommend that you compare the .onion address provided on the organization's Landing Page to the corresponding entry in this list, and verify that the addresses match before continuing. This provides a strong layer of defense against certain types of attacks that might try to trick you into visiting a malicious SecureDrop instance masquerading as a legitimate one. If you encounter a mismatch, please contact us at securedrop@freedom.press (GPG). This could be evidence of an attempted attack, or it could be a simple failure to communicate between an organization running SecureDrop and Freedom of the Press Foundation. In either case, we will investigate the matter and establish a path to resolution. Get involved!. Donate. Apache. https://www.apache.be/securedrop
flags: Yellow annotations circling the 'Apache' directory entry imply unstated significance - annotator's intent unverified

description: Photograph of page 225, Chapter Twelve ('The Secret Government'), of a book, captioned in white block letters 'FROM THE 1991 BOOK "BEHOLD THE PALE HORSE"' - i.e. Milton William Cooper's conspiracy book Behold a Pale Horse. A pink box highlights a passage claiming the government encouraged firearms imports for criminals and that the CIA, via drugs and hypnosis on mental patients in a process called 'Orion', induced schoolyard shootings to inflame the anti-gun lobby and end the 2nd Amendment. An author's note below, partly obscured by the caption, claims such incidents occurred nationwide and mentions the murder of Rabbi Meir Kahane. These are the book's claims, presented without evidence.
